Iceland Implements Temporary Tariffs on Transportation & Logistics Imports, Disrupting Industry Operations

Reykjavik – A sudden introduction of temporary tariffs on selected Transportation & Logistics products is causing ripples throughout Iceland’s logistics sector, with immediate effects being reported by industry leaders including Isavia Ohf.

The Ministry of Finance announced late Monday that a 12% tariff would be imposed on imported logistics equipment, such as cargo handling machinery, airport support vehicles, and certain spare parts, effective immediately. The move, which officials say is aimed at “protecting domestic infrastructure investments,” is set for an initial period of six months but may be extended pending review.

Isavia Ohf, which operates several of Iceland’s key transport hubs, confirmed on Wednesday that scheduled maintenance for critical ground support vehicles at Keflavik Airport has already been delayed due to increased costs and procurement uncertainty. “This measure has made it significantly more expensive to import essential equipment,” said Elín Jónsdóttir, the company’s head of logistics. “We are working closely with our suppliers and authorities to minimize operational disruptions, but delays are unavoidable at this stage.”

Industry observers warn that the tariffs may lead to a backlog in equipment upgrades and slowed modernization projects. “If these tariffs persist, we risk falling behind on efficiency and safety benchmarks,” said Hafsteinn Einarsson, spokesperson for the Icelandic Logistics Association. According to the association, average costs for new airport tow tractors have surged by up to 15% since the tariffs were enacted.

The Ministry of Finance has invited industry representatives to discussions next week, but as of Thursday, negotiations were ongoing and the tariffs remain in force. The Transportation & Logistics industry is closely monitoring developments as the situation evolves.
